title: Actual first-residue condition under constant scalar restriction
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of the l-adic field in Type u, X a Noetherian scheme in universe u, and K an arbitrary complex over its actual continuous integer coefficient ring [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. Transport and restrict K to the constant integer coefficients as in [def-sfb-integral-constant-model-realization] and [det-lem-integral-models-stacks]. The constant first residue reduction has constructible cohomology in every degree and finite Tor amplitude [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] if and only if the actual derivedReduction at index zero is bounded constructible and has finite Tor amplitude. No completeness of K is assumed.

proof.text: Apply internal_first_residue_reduction_comparison to get the residue coefficient isomorphism e and the natural common-quotient derived comparison c. At K, c identifies the constant first reduction M with F(L), where L is the actual first reduction and F is restriction along the inverse residue isomorphism.

Scalar restriction F is an additive exact equivalence and strong monoidal. In degree n, compose H^n(c) with the inverse exact homology comparison to identify H^n(M) with F(H^n(L)). Use the existing proved constantModel_comap_iff helper in IntegralConstantModelHeartClosure, which transports finite presentations, covers and strata along any condensed coefficient isomorphism. Transport along the preceding homology isomorphism with constantModelConstructible_transport. This proves equivalence of constructibility in every degree. These are the same finite constant-model definitions on both sides, so no conversion to finite-stalk constructibility is required.

F preserves flat objects. The source-library torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_obj_iff gives preservation and reflection of each Tor interval under F. Transport first along c, and then existentially quantify the endpoints. This identifies finite Tor amplitude of M and L. For finite Tor amplitude of L, homologyConcentratedIn_of_torAmplitudeIn tests with the unit; exists_homologyConcentratedIn_iff_bounded gives boundedness. Pair this with the preceding constructible homology. Conversely discard boundedness and reverse the two comparisons.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean assembly from one structural derived common-quotient comparison. Constructible homology, every Tor interval, and the boundedness implication are proved using existing coefficient-transport and derived-category lemmas.

theorem internal_residue_stacks_comparison
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (K : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X)) :
    IntegralModelsStacks.residueCondition.{u} l E X
      ((IntegralModelsStacks.restriction l E X).obj
          ((Mod.comap (coefficientMap
            (IntegralConstantModel.pointComparison l E).inv.hom X)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)) ↔
    constantModelBoundedConstructible (DerivedNakayama.quotientRing l E 1) X
      ((AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X 0).obj K) ∧
    DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude _
      ((AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X 0).obj K)
